As the Prophet rode into Khaybar his thigh was uncovered; after its conquest he took Safiya from Dihya, freed and married her, her freedom her mahr, with a wedding feast.
After praying Fajr in the dark the Prophet rode on Khaybar; its fighters were killed, women and children taken captive, and he married Safiya, her freedom being her dowry.
Serving the Prophet on the Khaibar expedition, Anas hears his prayers for refuge, sees him marry Safiya with a feast of hais, and hears him make Medina a sanctuary.
The Prophet attacked only after dawn, holding back if he heard the adhan; reaching Khaibar by night, he attacked at daybreak, saying Khaibar is ruined.
At Khaibar the people flee to their fort as the Prophet cries Allahu Akbar, Khaibar is ruined; later his announcer forbids donkey meat and the pots are overturned.
After Khaibar's conquest the Prophet questions the Jews about a poisoned sheep given him; they admit poisoning it to learn whether he was a liar or a prophet.
Reaching Khaybar in the early morning, the Prophet saw its people flee to their fort and said: Allah is Greater, Khaybar is ruined.
At Khaibar, Amir bin al-Akwa dies by his own blade yet earns a double reward; the Prophet attacks at dawn, forbids donkey meat, and frees and marries the captive Safiya.
A fierce fighter the Prophet says is of Hell kills himself; the Prophet bids the army lower their voices, heals Salama's wound, and gives Ali the flag for Khaibar's conquest.
Khaibar's governor must not swap poor dates for fewer fine ones; its Jews farm it for half the crop, Muslims finally eat their fill, and a poisoned sheep is presented.
Anas, serving the Prophet, often heard him seek refuge from worry and debt; returning from Khaibar he held Safiyya's wedding feast, said Uhud loves us, and declared Medina a sanctuary.
Besieging Khaibar, Abdullah bin Mughaffal went to take a skin of fat thrown down, then, seeing the Prophet behind him, held back out of shyness.
After Khaibar's conquest the Prophet questioned the Jews about a poisoned roasted sheep given him; they admitted poisoning it to learn whether he was a liar or a prophet.
Some said Amir, killed at Khaibar, lost his deeds by killing himself, but the Prophet said whoever says so lies, for Amir has a double reward.
